learning_outcomes.text: Understand the importance of separation operations in chemical engineering.
Learn different separation processes such as evaporation, distillation, liquid-liquid extraction, and solid-liquid extraction.
Learn graphical calculation methods for binary systems: McCabe-Thiele diagram, Ponchon-Savarit diagram, and triangular diagram.
Ability to establish mass and energy balances during the design of evaporation, distillation, and extraction.
Ability to analyze separation process problems in chemical engineering.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to Separation Processes, Evaporator Auxiliary Components
Types of Evaporators, Design of Single Effect Evaporator
Design of Multiple Effect Evaporators, Vapor Compression Evaporators
Batch and Flash Distillation, Continuous Distillation, McCabe-Thiele Method
Total Reflux, Minimum Reflux and Tray Efficiency
Equilibrium Relations in Multicomponent Distillation, Bubble and Dew Point Calculation
Bubble and Dew Point Calculation, Estimation Methods in Multicomponent Design
bibliography: C. J. Geankoplis, “Transport Processes and Separation Process (Includes Unit Operations)”, Prentice Hall, 4th Edition, 2003.
W. McCabe, J. Smith, P. Harriott, “Unit Operations of Chemical Engineering”, McGraw-Hill, 7th Edition, 2005.
R. E. Treybal, “Mass-Transfer Operations”, McGraw-Hill, 3rd Edition, 1981.
